utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Case Number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have the appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Goods afternoon, Your Honours, counsel and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Matthias Neuner, and Darryl Mundis, assisted by Andres Vatter, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the appearances for Defence counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President, good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of General Enver Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, lead counsel, and Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the appearances for the other Defence team, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and our legal assistant, Nermin Mulalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will now be resuming on the 2nd of May, 2005, after having had a brief break. I would like to greet members of the Prosecution, Defence counsel, General Hadzihasanovic, and Brigadier Kubura. And I wouldn't want to forget to mention everyone else in and around the courtroom. As I have said, we will be resuming with the proceedings today. We're going straight ahead now. We only have a few witnesses left to hear. We have been provided with Mr. Kubura's Defence counsel's planning schedule. We have three witnesses scheduled, one today, two on Tuesday, and perhaps we will be continuing on Wednesday. This means that we won't be having a witness for Thursday. Is this, in fact, the schedule submitted by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. That is the correct schedule. We will be calling one witness today and we intended to call another witness tomorrow. Mr. Dixon will be conducting the examination-in-chief. If everything goes as planned, we'll call the second witness on that day, who should complete his testimony on Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: (redacted). We've also received submissions from the Prosecution, written submissions, that concern the motion to re-open their case to have certain documents admitted into evidence. Defence counsel will provide us with their submissions as soon as possible. At the Status Conference, approximate planning -- a schedule was presented by the Chamber's legal officer, and it appears that the parties have said that they will try to abide by this schedule. In theory, this means that the proceedings should be completed by mid-July. If there are no other issues to be raised, we will now call the witness into the courtroom. No issues to be raised by the Prosecution or by Defence counsel? In that case, we'll call the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, sir. I'd first like to make sure that you are receiving the interpretation of what I'm saying into your own language. If so, please say that you can hear and understand me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear and understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you have been called here as a witness for Brigadier Kubura's Defence counsel. Before you take the solemn declaration, I would be grateful if you could tell me your first and last names, your date and place of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Kasim Alajbegovic. I was born on the 24th of December, 1963, in Groce -- in the village of Groce, in the municipality of Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your current job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a graduated mechanical engineer. I work in a public company, Grinje [phoen] in Kakanj, which is involved in distributing energy in the town and in the surrounding areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1992 and 1993, what position did you hold? Were you a member of the military at the time? If so, which unit were you a member of and what rank or position did you have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the beginning of 1992, I was a member of the reserve police force. I was assigned to that force, and then sometime in July 1992 we were resubordinated to the command of the Kakanj municipal Territorial Defence Staff. I was assigned a position in the staff command, and I was responsible for logistics. Around October, I was given the task of establishing a battalion, the future 7th Muslim Brigade what was part of the ABiH army. Initially in that unit, I was the commander until the 22nd of February, 1993, when I requested professionally trained officer and I was assigned as deputy commander and remained in that post until the 8th of June, 1993, when I was wounded and sent to hospital for medical treatment. I was mobilised [as interpreted] -- I was mobilised in September 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you already testified before an international or national court with regard to the events that took place in your country in 1992 or 1993 or is this the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time I have been in a court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please read out the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly swear that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may sit down. Before I give the floor to the Defence, who will be conducting their examination-in-chief, I would like to provide you with some information about the procedure that we will be following. This is something that I do whenever a witness appears in the courtroom. Initially, you will have to answer the questions put to you by Brigadier Kubura's Defence, and you have certainly met his Defence in the course of your proofing. Once this stage has been completed, the Prosecution, who are to your right, will conduct what we call the cross-examination. Having completed their cross-examination, Defence counsel, who are to your left, may ask you additional questions. I would also like to point out that General Hadzihasanovic's Defence counsel, since they are a separate party, they may also put questions to you. Then the three Judges, who are sitting in front of you, may ask you questions if they believe that it is necessary, either in order to clarify some of your answers or because the Judges believe that it is in the interest of justice to put some questions to you since the Judges may feel that there are certain gaps in your testimony. If the Judges put questions to a witness, the Prosecution and Defence counsel may take the floor again and put other questions to you to clarify some of the answers that you have provided to the Judges. You may not be aware of this fact, or perhaps you are aware of the fact, that the procedure followed here is mainly oral and you will see in front of you a monitor on which everything that is said is transcribed. As the procedure followed is oral, try to provide full answers to the questions put to you because your answers will form the evidence, the testimony. You might be shown certain documents, perhaps military documents; and you might be asked to say whether you are familiar with them, whether you were familiar with them in 1992 or 1993; and you might be shown documents that you yourself drafted. There are two or points that I need to draw your attention to. You have taken the solemn declaration, which means you should not give false testimony. As you know, false testimony is an offence which is punishable by the Tribunal. In addition, I should also point out something that is specific to this procedure. When you answer a question, if you believe that your answer could be used against you at a subsequent date, since the information could be used to prosecute you, you may refuse to answer the question. In such exceptional circumstances, the Chamber can compel you to answer the question but the Chamber grants you immunity, which means that whatever you say cannot be used against you. But rest assured, we have never had such a situation to date. If you encounter any difficulties in the course of proceedings, don't hesitate to inform us of the fact; we are here to resolve any difficulties. We will be having two breaks today, two 25-minute breaks. We have to have breaks for technical reasons, since it's necessary to change the tapes and it's also necessary for you to have a rest, because you will see that answers questions incessantly can be quite tiring and it's necessary for witnesses to have a brief 25 to 30-minute break. If you fail to understand a question, don't hesitate to ask the party putting the question to you to rephrase it because it's necessary for to you fully understand the questions put to you, and it is also necessary for your answer to the questions to be appropriate. This is how we will be proceeding and the hearing will end at 1900 hours. I will now give the floor to Brigadier Kubura's Defence counsel for the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, in response to a question to the Presiding Judge, you told us what you did and where you were in 1992 and 1993, but for the sake of the transcript, I think that in the transcript it said that you were mobilised in 1993. But I believe that you said that you were demobilised in September 1993.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I was demobilised from the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of the war in 1992, in April 1992, were you in Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: During that period, after the beginning of the war, were you the commander of some unit that had been established in Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the period after the aggression?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: After the beginning of the aggression and before the 7th Brigade was established.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we just have two documents we would like to use, and with your leave, I would like to show these two documents to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at the document dated October 1992 -- in fact, the 5th of November, 1992. It's a list of men who were mobilised. Have a look at the document and tell us what the document is and who the individuals on the list are, but first of all tell us whether you recognise the document.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with this document. At this time, the battalion had not yet been established, but there were men out of whom independent platoons were established through the municipal secretariat for defence, which was involved in carrying out the mobilisation. And this was done with agreement of the command of the municipal defence staff, which was part of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. This is a list of men who were members of the independent Trsce Detachment -- Platoon.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And since these are men who were very young at the time and hadn't served in the JNA, in the Yugoslav Peoples' Army. And before engaging them in combat, it was necessary to provide them with basic training.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the person who signed the document, Fadil Imamovic? Do you know who this person is?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: This is the Chief of Staff, Fadil Imamovic, who carried out those duties in the Kakanj municipal staff at the time. I know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did these men at any point in time become members of the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. These men subsequently became members of the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When was the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade formed?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: When we talk about the formation of any units and battalions, and that goes for the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade, well in the course of that period you have a certain period of time where certain preparations must be made, and such preparations include the document that I've just referred to. And at that time, since we had no battalion, we were -- or rather, we carried out all our tasks with the approval of the command of the municipal defence staff. And then in the month of December, and that already refers to the second document I believe, so in December, following an order, we created the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade whereupon we got our own seal and stamp and then we were allowed to carry out the relevant duties having to do with the setting up of the battalion, of course, with the approval of our superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This document number two, I mean the second document that you looked at, does it illustrate what you've just explained? Does it refer to the setting up of the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the document in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where was the 3rd Battalion stationed, the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The first location was in a village of Doboj, near Kakanj, at the primary school. This was a the area, or rather a facility that had been offered to us, and of course we accepted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay there and where did you move later?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Since the school had to be vacated for the purposes of the school activity proper, the War Presidency of the municipality of Kakanj at some point, if I remember correctly, I think it was in the month of March - it was still quite cold, there was no heating at the hotel - but they offered us the premises at the hotel or motel, as it used to be called, Sretno in Kakanj. And initially it had been built as a hotel or restaurant, and so it was not convenient for us but we had no choice, we had to take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain what you mean when you say it's not convenient?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, barracks for soldiers are never built on the motorway or the ramps for getting on and off the motorway or in valleys where there are mountains very close to you and possibly there could be a threat coming -- an armed threat coming from those mountains. So what I mean, it is a good location for a hotel, but when we are talking about barracks in terms of security, it is inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me about the soldiers who joined the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade, where were they from? What area did they come from?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The 3rd Battalion was, for the most part, manned by local people from the area of the municipality of Kakanj, and about 99 per cent of them were local people from Kakanj and they all knew one another, we all knew one another. And perhaps there were a couple of people who were refugees, temporarily residing at Kakanj, but for the most part we are talking about Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In terms of the actual formation, what was the manning strength and -- of this battalion when you were commander in 1993?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, our desire and our goal was to set up a mountain battalion; however, in terms of manning strength, we can say that we were only working at a capacity of about 35 per cent. So our companies, what we called companies, had about 55 people each. We had two companies and what we called a command for battalion. So all in all, between 120 and 130 members whilst I was there, and we called the formation the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade. Obviously our housing facilities or the MTS that we had at our disposal did not allow us to arrive at the level of a battalion in terms of manning strength either.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When did you become commander of this battalion?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: De facto, I became commander at the very beginning, I mean at the time when this list of young men was being drawn up. We had no premises or anything at the time. I used to work at the command of the municipal defence staff, which means that I was in charge of these types of tasks. So there is no clear dividing line, but I became commander whilst this battalion was in the process of being set up, so I was the first commander basically. So if we refer to the order about the setting up of the battalion and the battalion coming in existence and from the very start, I was the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Until when did you remain commander and for what reason did you not stay in that position?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I was educated in mechanic engineering; I'm an engineer. So in terms of defending the country from aggression and making my own contribution in the course of that process, I've joined in simply in order to protect my family and to protect the area, the country, that I was living in. So I was not trained to carry out these tasks, war-related duties, I mean defence, command, and all that. And following my own personal request, I was asked for professional officer to be sent down and to take up this post of commander, and I accepted that I could act as an assistant for those duties that that future commander would think appropriate that I should do. And I think about -- I must have remained in the post of commander until the 22nd of February; and after that, I was the deputy commander of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Line 10 -- or rather page 10, line 20, for the sake of the transcript, I would just like to repeat the question when you referred to the members of the 3rd Battalion. My understanding was that you said that all members of the battalion were Bosniaks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where were the soldiers of the 3rd Battalion trained, and what sort of training was that?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: It was necessary to have certain training, but we did not have the necessary conditions for such activity. For this reason, we had to make due which means that in between combat activity, we tried to train people, mostly at the Doboj school when we were there in classrooms or at the gym. And the other part of this training, mostly in terms of marches and orientation exercises, et cetera, would take them out into the mountains above Kakanj and pretty close to this school in Doboj, because we did not really want to provoke or irritate or disturb the local population. And we didn't want either to disturb them or to be disturbed by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And in the course of that period of time when you were commander of this battalion, was the battalion involved in any combat activity and was it stationed in the area or was spending time in the area of Bijelo Bucje, if you are familiar with the area at all.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course I'm very familiar with the area of Bijelo Bucje because I was there with the army at Bijelo Bucje -- well, the army was there in January and February. So one group was there in January and another group went up in February.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Were members of your battalion involved in any combat activity in the area or were they just holding the Defence lines, can you clarify, please?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Our task was to monitor the line at Bijelo Bucje, that is to say just above the village of Bijelo Bucje; that was our exclusive task as it were. And in the course of our stay there, there were no attacks coming from the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Throughout your time with the battalion, you were first commander and then deputy commander. As the commanding officer, were you receiving any sort of pay, wages, something like that?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I did not. And the fighters, members of the 3rd Battalion, did not get any wages in money, in cash. What we did get -- well, we used to receive some of the basic staple foods, as it were, as much as it was possible to provide that, and that applied to all the other army units. They were in the same situation, the other brigades, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Alajbegovic, I'd like to move on to a different topic now. So Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. I'm going to ask you whether you've heard at some point in May 1993 about certain incidents taking place in Kakanj, mid-May 1993, and can you tell us what those incidents were all about?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I did hear that at some point mid-1993, an incident took place at Kakanj. There was something between the brigade military police and the members of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, what actually happened mid-May 1993?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: What I know is that members of military police were supposed to bring in or detain certain members of the 7th Brigade who, after their leave, did not report back on duty to their units of origin. And also, they were driving somewhere in the direction of the power plant, in the direction of those villages. When passing through a village, which we at Kakanj called Rampa [phoen], they came across members of HVO and there was some shooting, and that information reached the barracks through the members of military police who managed to return to barracks where they informed us that several military police members had been detained in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what happened afterwards?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, whilst all this was going on, I was not in the barracks myself, I was in town. And upon my return at some point in early evening, I was told about these military policemen who had come back, apparently out of fear of their colleagues who had been taken prisoner, been killed, that they had taken a certain number of the members of the HVO from the nearby village. And I think the village was called Povezice. There is a railway station there. Having heard what had happened, I got in touch with the command of the 309th Brigade, and Kakanj was in their area of responsibility. My intention was to establish some sort of contact with the HVO command in Kakanj and to start talks, to start negotiations, in order to avoid any undesirable situations and in order for people on both sides to be released.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the commander of the 309th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, the commander of the 309th Brigade was Dzemal Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of this commander having taken any steps in order to try and solve this problem, to resolve this situation?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he got in touch with the HVO commander Neven Maric, I believe that -- I don't know whether it was the French UNPROFOR Battalion or who, but they apparently found out about this incident pretty soon and they got involved in these talks, but I myself was not present.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether these negotiations were held?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: At the time they said they had been held. The information we were provided with confirmed the fact that they had been held.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: On that day or later on, did you receive any information on the outcome of those negotiations?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: We were then told that people who'd been detained in that part of the settlement had been released as a result of UNPROFOR action, and one member of the military police had been escorted by UNPROFOR and he was wounded. I really don't know what sort of wounds he had.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Is this a military policeman from the 7th Muslim Brigade or the HVO?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: He was a member of the brigade military police from the 7th Muslim Brigade. All these policemen were released late in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Afterwards, did you hear anything about the HVO members being released?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The brigade military police, after that event, I think it was on the following day, they released the members that they had captured in order to organise an exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether on that day or later on, Mr. Kubura stayed in Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Amir Kubura didn't stay in Kakanj on that day or on the following day. He did not appear in the barracks where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You say he didn't appear in the barracks on that day. As a rule when someone from the command brigade in Zenica came to the barracks, would the battalion command be aware of the fact or was some other procedure followed?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, usually, the battalion command would be aware of the fact that someone from the brigade command was coming. It wouldn't be possible for someone to come in secret without having announced his visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Alajbegovic, sometime in the beginning of June 1993, was your battalion engaged in combat in the Ovnak sector?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Our battalion was engaged in combat in the Ovnak sector at the beginning of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You were then the deputy commander?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In what way and how many battalion members reached the Ovnak sector?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: In the area of deployment, which is near Ovnak -- well, about a hundred of us arrived in that area, about a hundred combatants arrived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: How were the troops transported there?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: They were driven there in buses from Kakanj; from Kakanj to Zenica; and then from Zenica, buses took them to deployment area in the vicinity of Ovnak.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where were the members of your battalion billeted when you arrived in the Ovnak sector?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Our men were billeted in the Pojske area, in the village of Pojske.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with your leave, we would like to use a map. Perhaps the witness could indicate the position of the 3rd Battalion on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you first show us where the village of Pojske is. You might need a little time to find it. Could you draw a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks] This is the village of Pojske.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark it with number 1; this will enable us to follow everything.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Upon arriving in the village of Pojske, what happened, Mr. Alajbegovic?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Upon arriving in the village of Pojske, I think it was on the 6th of June, the troops were deployed in the village. And on the 7th, an attempt was made to raid the blockade of the road, but the 3rd Battalion didn't participate in this action. On the 8th of June, part of the battalion remained in the Crni Vrh area with the 2nd Battalion and another unit, one company, went to the Strmac axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where were you, Mr. Alajbegovic?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I was on the Strmac axis with this unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you have a look at the map and indicate the location of Strmac.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks] The Strmac elevation. Should I mark it with a number?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mark it with number 2.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When did combat start on that day and when did it end, the combat that your battalion was involved in?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of June, the fighting started in the morning. The task was to take the Strmac elevation. The fighting continued throughout the day, and in the afternoon between 3.00 and 3.30 p.m. I was wounded. I was wounded at the Strmac elevation, and I was then evacuated and taken to the Zenica hospital where I was provided with medical treatment; and I was then transferred to Kakanj. In Kakanj I went to the barracks to obtain information on the situation and I think that I spent that night at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: All of this took place on the 8th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the 8th of June. According to the information I obtained after I was wounded, half an hour or an hour later, I obtained information according to which the Strmac elevation had fallen; it had been taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did members of your battalion -- were members of your battalion engaged in settlements in inhabited settlements? Did you enter inhabited settlements, such as the ones you have marked on this map?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Our main -- my main task was to assume control of certain elevations and to secure the road passing through Ovnak.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I'll repeat my question. Was there any fighting in inhabited villages?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The fighting was on the Strmac elevation. This is a hill that's covered in forest, it's a mountain, in fact. That's where there was fighting, only in that area. There were no houses in the vicinity. The Strmac hill is covered in forest, and then to the left there was a sort of clearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Since you were wounded, you went to Zenica and then you arrived in Kakanj on that very same day. What was the situation in Kakanj like when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: In the barracks, I obtained some information, and what I was told was not very positive. I was told that HVO members had stepped up their activity on the elevations, increased numbers of HVO members were going there, and the security situation in Kakanj was very worrying.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any indications that there would be fighting?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: That was on the 8th. And what I found out in the command of the 309th Brigade, since that was its zone of responsibility, members of the 7th Brigade were in the field, but according to what I found out there, in the furthest-removed villages towards Vares which were under the control of the HVO, they had already started torching certain features. I think the village is called Kracici. The inhabitants from that area, from that village, had asked for protection and it wasn't possible to reach that village because the HVO controlled the route of access to the village from the surrounding hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When did the members of your battalion return to Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The information that we had was forwarded and sent to the -- into the field where the troops were located. And on the 9th, they arrived in Kakanj in the evening. They were taken there in an organised manner in vehicles, and they went to the barracks to resupply themselves with materiel and technical equipment. And then vehicles took them to the village of Zagradje which is to the north of Kakanj; it's about 5 or 6 kilometres to the north of Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did the men have the possibility of going home once they had arrived in the barracks, or did they immediately did to Zagradje, the village that you have just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The soldiers stayed in the barracks for as long as it was necessary in order to resupply themselves with the necessary amount of materiel and technical equipment, which they needed to engage in forthcoming combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did they go to their homes at all, or did they go to carry out a new task from the barracks?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't go home. They didn't have time to go home, in particular since many of the villages that the men were from could not be reached, because the area in which their houses were located was under HVO control on the whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where were you when the soldiers arrived?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I was in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see them arriving?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Were you present when they set off in the direction of the village of Zagradje?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where the village of Zagradje is located?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The village of Zagradje is inhabited by Bosniaks alone; it's 5 to 6 kilometres to the north of Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with your leave, since the witness knows where this village is located and this village has been mentioned on a number of occasions in the course of the proceedings, with your leave, we would like to ask the witness to mark the location of this village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I number them?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In whose area of responsibility is this village, Zagradje?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The question is in the area of the municipality of Kakanj, and at the time, it was in the area covered by the 309th Brigade. It was the brigade which is actually domiciled, stationed, in Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, Mr. President, I would like the witness to sign both maps and date them as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You can put your signature in the white part of the document, and please could you date them as well.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you meet Mr. Kubura and when? In what way did you meet? How long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I met Mr. Amir Kubura in December 1992 whilst he was carrying out the duty -- I believe the duty of the commander of the battalion which belonged to the 333rd Brigade, and it was at the open-cast mine near Kakanj because at the time, we had certain joint activities under the command of the municipal defence staff in the direction of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you meet him whilst he was a member of the 7th Brigade -- I mean, did you ever meet with him in the course of that period of time?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what duty, what function, he had within the 7th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: During the period of time that I was a member as well, we tended to address Amir Kubura as chief of -- as chief. He was the Chief of Staff. And afterwards, when I was receiving medical treatment by the end of that period when I was about to be demobilised, I heard at some point in August, I believe, that he had been appointed commander of the 7th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question to conclude. Were you at any point in time the first man, the chief of the municipality of Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: By the end of 1999, the high representative replaced the then-municipal chief of Kakanj, and in the course of that period between January and May, I carried out the duties of the municipal chief in Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: As the first man of the municipality of Kakanj, did you ever have any contacts with Croat representatives of the Croat population returning to Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Of course. There were certain projects that I worked on together with Mr. Niko Lozancic who, at the time, was the presiding officer of the house of representatives of the federation. And also with Franjo Petricevic, who at the time was minister for the economics, agriculture, and mining in the canton that the municipality of Kakanj belongs to. It was a period of very intense implementation of the Dayton Accord. More specifically, a period in which property was being returned - when I say "property," I mostly mean housing, residential property - it was being returned to prewar occupants and owners, as well as a period of cooperation in the field of culture on the basis of certain associations which were also Croatian associations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This is a bit of a sensitive issue, but what was the general assessment of your work?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: If we can talk about assessment, I was accountable to the municipal council which had appointed me in the first place, and my proposal, starting from the budgetary proposals and everything else, used to be approved unanimously. And apart from Bosniaks, there were other members, Croat members, sitting on that council.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When I asked this question, what I meant what was the assessment of your work on the part of the Croat population and the Croat dignitaries?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I remember the congratulations -- and actually at the same time, it was an invitation to attend a gathering organised by a Croat cultural society called Napredak, Progress. And they both congratulated me on my election to the post of municipal chief at Kakanj and wishing me all the best in the course of my term of office, saying that they wish me a great deal of success and they hope that I would be as fair as I used to be before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That concludes our examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right then. Before the break, the other lawyers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we do have a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Alajbegovic, in your answer to my learned colleague's questions, you mentioned in the month of May an incident took place. On that occasion, HVO took prisoner a certain number of military police officers of the 7th Muslim Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Prior to that, both Croats and Muslims in Kakanj used to co-exist and live together without any major incidents, and together with the commander of the 309th Mountain Brigade you tried to resolve the situation relating to this incident as soon as possible; is that the correct assessment?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you've already told my colleague, on the very next day there was the exchange of prisoners. What I would like you to tell me, Mr. Alajbegovic, is: Is it correct that no one or none of the Croatian prisoners or their families had ever complained about being treated unfairly and that you had never received any formal complaint or report in this respect?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely. I was not aware of any such complaints, and I lived in the area afterwards and nobody came forward and nobody complained of any sort of injustice or unfairness in the course of that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So basically, the only things you found out was that UNPROFOR brought in, on a stretcher, one member of the 7th Muslim Brigade who was -- on the occasion of that operation, who had been beaten up by the HVO members; is that the only piece of information that you received?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I had heard that he had been beaten up, but actually I was told that he was wounded. And I had never seen him, so I don't know what sort of injuries he had.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I just have a number of shorter questions now. Can you tell me if you knew at the time who was the commander of the 3rd Corps, within which the 7th Muslim Brigade was included?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of that period of time, I believe that it was Mr. Enver Hadzihasanovic. And so at that time, as deputy commander, I was never in touch with anyone else -- I mean I was in touch with the commander of the battalion, and then it was up to him. So I can't really say with any degree of certainty.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, in the course of the period of time that you spent within the 3rd Battalion, you never met with Mr. Hadzihasanovic in Kakanj, you never met him and you never saw him in Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: All I know about Mr. Hadzihasanovic is that his family was somewhere near Kakanj or in Kakanj, but I've never come across him personally in Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And to conclude, in conjunction with this period of time in the month of June, you said that whilst you, the armed forces from Kakanj, were engaged in combat operations at Ovnak, the HVO took hold of dominant elevations around Kakanj and were -- that they were occupying those positions in stronger numbers. And that's the information that you received when you came back that evening?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And prior to that, you had encountered numerous incidents provoked by the HVO in the area of Kakanj and within Kakanj, but you and the 309th Brigade both tried to avoid any confrontation and to make sure that all those incidents could be resolved peacefully and smoothed out; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Only when HVO started attacking and torching the villages inhabited by Muslim population, such as on the 9th of June, there was an all-out confrontation with HVO; is that what you said in reply to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. questions put to you by my colleagues?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right then. It's 25 to. We shall have a break now and we'll continue at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing continues. I'm going to give the floor to the Prosecution for the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Alajbegovic. My name is Matthias Neuner, and I'm appearing here along with my colleagues on behalf of the Prosecution. I'm going to put a couple of questions to you, and if you don't understand one of these questions, please ask me to repeat it or to rephrase it if necessary. Do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: After 22nd February, 1993, a commander took over command of the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. Was the name of this commander Nihad Catic?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, his name was Nihad Catic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And throughout your service for the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, did Mr. Nihad Catic remain your superior?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, after that period -- when he arrived, yes, he was my superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And until the end of your service, including the Ovnak operation, Mr. Catic was your commander?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: As you -- as an acting commander, did also Mr. Nihad Catic report in the first half of 1993 on the one hand side to the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade and on the other hand side to the 3rd Corps command?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The command of the battalion was accountable to the command of the 7th Muslim Brigade; they were their superiors. And the 7th Muslim Brigade was within the framework of the 3rd Corps of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did it happen also that reports were sent from the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, 3rd Battalion commander, directly to the 3rd Corps command, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I think that during the time that I was commander, I don't think it ever happened and I don't suppose it happened when we had another commander at the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, may I have document Prosecution Exhibit P533 distributed. We have copies for everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is a report on the 3rd battalion work and implementation of tasks dating 8 March 1993. And, Witness, I ask you to look only at the first page, and if you look to at the "sent to" section on the lower left-hand side of the first page, do you see that this 3rd Battalion report is being sent to the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade command as well as to the command of the 3rd Corps? Can you please just confirm.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: This document that is being shown to me is apparently signed by the commander of the 3rd Battalion Nihad, probably Catic, it's under the stamp. And apparently it was submitted to the superior command of the 7th Brigade [as interpreted]; and one copy the signatory kept for himself, and one was filed in the archive.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The document may be removed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Within --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I see my learned colleague on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I think that my learned colleague asked whether it was provided to the 3rd Corps. I don't know if that's an error in the transcript. The witness only said it was sent to the command of the 3rd Brigade and the command of the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In 1993 in the first half, you were, after the 22nd of February, deputy commander of the 3rd Battalion and Mr. Catic was commander. Can you please confirm, there was no position of Chief of Staff within the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, in the battalion there was no Chief of Staff at that time, not in the part that I was in command of. As to whether there was such a person at is subsequent date, I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: However, on the level of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, the brigade level itself, there was the position of a Chief of Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was the position of the Chief of Staff within the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So while on the brigade level, there was a Chief of Staff, no such position was contained or provided for on the battalion level, especially not on the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade? Can you please confirm.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: In the mountain battalion, as far as I can remember, there was no Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You refer to mountain battalion, you're referring to your 3rd Battalion, or are you referring to all three battalions of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade which did not have a position of Chief of Staff? Please clarify.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I'm talking about the 3rd Battalion. As for the other ones, I'm not familiar with the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to ask you whether you know Mr. Saban Zunic, Z-u-n-i-c, Mr. Saban Zunic; have you ever heard his name?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember having heard that name. I don't remember Saban Zunic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to switch to March 1993, and you mentioned that the 3rd Battalion moved to Motel Sretno. What I wanted to ask you: Was also the 3rd Battalion command moving to Motel Sretno in March 1993?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The entire unit moved out of the school and moved into Motel Sretno.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Motel Sretno was a building with several floors. On which of these floors was the command, the battalion command, located post-March 1993?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: There were two offices on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You're referring to two offices. Are you referring to your own office also and also to the office of Mr. Nihad Catic?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: There was Nihad Catic's office, and there was another small office which I would occasionally use; and these two offices were on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So people -- persons who entered Motel Sretno, did they have to pass by the battalion command's offices, or were these two offices you just described more distant, meaning somewhere in the back of the ground floor, so that visitors didn't pass by upon entering the building?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: There were several entrances, or rather, exits that Motel Sretno had since this was a catering establishment. So people entering the building or leaving the building could use any of those entrances.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm just trying to clarify. So if you -- was there a main entrance, first of all, which was usually used and what was the position of the command's office in relation to that main entrance, if there was any?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the main entrance, the offices were to the right of the main entrance. They were behind the hotel reception desk. It was not possible to see who was entering or leaving the hotel from the offices if the doors were closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was there also a part in Motel Sretno where a kind of temporary warehouse was established, where goods, MTS items, could be stored; and if so, where was it?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The motel had a part which was used as a warehouse. Goods would be delivered to that part behind the motel, behind the main entrance. I think that that was the part used as a warehouse, and there was another part that we used for the little materiel and technical equipment that we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was there also a facility where prisoners -- if any were taken, where prisoners could be kept in Motel Sretno?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was no area in which would be used to detain individuals who would have the status of some kind of a prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Does this imply that prisoners weren't held in Motel Sretno at all, or at least at some point in time temporarily prisoners were hold -- were held in Motel Sretno in the first half of 1993?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, given the information that I had during the period when there was an incident that concerned obtaining the release of the members of the military police who had been captured -- as far as I know, the military policemen who managed to escape capture, and they brought in a certain number of HVO members. I don't know the identity of the individuals they brought in, nor do I know how many individuals were brought in. I did not see them, nor did I know which part of the hotel they were being kept in at the time, but I heard that a certain number of HVO members had been brought in. So as far as the details are concerned, as far as the accommodation they had, et cetera, there is nothing that I could tell you. I wasn't present there. All I know is what I heard from others when I returned to the barracks. I was focused on establishing negotiations and on trying to resolve the difficulty we had run into in a peaceful manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You mentioned military policemen who took prisoners. Were these military policemen of the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade or military policemen attached directly to the brigade, meaning military policemen from Zenica, do you know?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: When I refer to military policemen, I'm referring to the brigade military policemen who set off to carry out their task which was to bring in members of the 7th Brigade who had failed to report back to the brigade after they had been granted leave. And when I'm referring to this group of men, it's necessary to distinguish two components: We have the men who were captured by the HVO, and the other component concerns the policemen that managed to escape when the shooting broke out and they managed to return to the hotel. As far as bringing individuals in is concerned, the military policemen who managed to return brought in HVO members; they were the ones who brought in HVO members. The battalion only had two or three policemen that mainly provided security for the building, for the entrances, et cetera. These were the regular duties that they had to perform at the main entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So the military policemen which, on the 18th of May, 1993, captured, as you put it, HVO members, these military police members are distinct from others who just were on sentry duty, who guarded Motel Sretno? Can you just clarify, please.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Certainly. You, as far as I understood your answer, made a distinction among the military policemen, and I'm personally only interested in military policemen who, as you put it, escaped being arrested themselves and who subsequently took, as you put it, HVO members prisoners. These military policemen who captured HVO men on the 18th of May, 1993, these military policemen, were they coming from Zenica or were they employed constantly in the 3rd Battalion in Kakanj to guard the building? Can you just clarify, please.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: HVO members were captured by members of the brigade military police who managed to avoid being captured, so the battalion military police did not bring these men in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification. How did the brigade military -- or when did the brigade military policemen arrive? Did they arrive on the 18th of May, to the best of your recollection, or a day or two earlier? What do you know?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: They arrived there on that day, on the 18th, in the afternoon. Everything took place very rapidly. One might say that everything took place within an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, who had sent these military policemen on the 18th in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know whether they reported to anybody in the 3rd Battalion on the 18th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You, yourself, stated you were in town on the 18th of May, 1993, and you arrived in the evening at Motel Sretno. Can you clarify what you mean by "evening." What time, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember when they arrived, but there was the shooting that had broken out and HVO members had already been brought in. In fact, that is when I found out about what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So who told you, upon return to Motel Sretno, what had happened and what were you told?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: All of this happened a long time ago so it's difficult for me to remember such details, but I think that one of the soldiers I met on the grounds at the hotel provided me with this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This moment when you returned from -- to Motel Sretno, who was the most senior officer at Motel Sretno?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you speak to Nihad Catic on that evening?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: We were both trying to establish contact with the HVO through the intermediary of the command of the 309th -- through the intermediary of all those who could assist in resolving the difficulties in order to avoid other negative consequences.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who was the senior person among the military police from the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in Zenica on the 18th of May at Motel Sretno? Who was the most senior person among this -- from this group?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I did not personally know those military policemen. I didn't know any of them, and I don't know whether there was an officer among them or perhaps it was just a group of military policemen. These people, these men, were not from Kakanj, they were from Zenica. When they arrived, I was not in the barracks. They didn't report to me, so I wasn't in a position to know whether there was anyone who had a high rank or a low rank. I didn't even know how many of them there were. I didn't know these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How long that evening did you stay in Motel Sretno?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how long I stayed there that evening. I know that I was in contact with this brigade. I don't know when, but it was quite late in the evening when I went home to stay the night there, and that is about 5 kilometres from Kakanj; that is where my home was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you went home late in the evening. Until you went home, were there more persons brought to Motel Sretno from outside? I'm referring to persons who were detained.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: During that time, no people were brought in except for the ones who had been brought in before, I mean I've mentioned the military police before.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, who was in charge of the persons detained that evening?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: My activity was aimed at obtaining certain information and mobilising people to start negotiating and getting in touch with these people. So no special attention was being paid, at least on my part as deputy commander, to who exactly was in charge of the detained persons. I wouldn't be able to tell you, really. So the military police were present there and whilst the -- waiting for the return of the other police officers and to have this exchange with regard to the detained HVO members.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You said you dealt with contacting negotiators. What was your commander, Mr. Nihad Catic, doing that evening?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: He was involved in the same job.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So both of you paid attention to the outside, meaning the negotiations, and you paid less attention to what was going inside Motel Sretno; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he was involved as commander because he was not from Kakanj, and I, myself, was from Kakanj. And I was better acquainted with these people as the commander of the 390th [as interpreted] Brigade, and so that's why I was drafted in as well. And so we were focussing on these negotiations for the release of the military police members in order to be able to have this exchange of prisoners and take things back to the way they were before.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know whether a guerilla group was in the Motel Sretno that evening?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: What guerilla group are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm referring to a guerilla group, Mountain Guerilla or Planina Guerilla which, according to a document, was sent to the 3rd Battalion command in Kakanj. This is Prosecution Exhibit P681, and the stamp on the document is the 19th of May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Except for the military police, I did not see at the hotel anyone else. I didn't see anyone else, other than the military police from the 7th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So on the 19th of May, were you also at Motel Sretno and you also didn't see a guerilla group?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, may have Exhibit P -- oh, I withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You talked about the negotiations in which you were directly or indirectly involved. These negotiations, did they go on on the 19th of May at this thermoelectric power plant in Catici? Please confirm.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: When I referred to negotiations, what I'm talking about is activities which were underway a couple of hours after this incident and immediately after the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And do you know where these negotiations took place?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I was told that certain talks were being held. I wouldn't know where exactly, but where I was, it was the command of the 309th Brigade, but I don't know whether anything was taking place anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When the negotiations were finally successful, the prisoners or the detainees were exchanged. Who took the prisoners out of Motel Sretno in order to have them exchanged; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't. I did not see the detainees. I did not see them and I don't know who released them from the motel, and I don't even know how many there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, can I please have P728 distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The only reason for having this document distributed is: Can you please confirm that this is your signature? It's a document dating from or stamped on the 19th of April, 1993, so a month before the events we just discussed about. Is that your signature, please?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You're talking here in the heading -- or you address this document to the chief of the 7th Muslim Brigade. Can you state who was the chief to whom you wanted to send this document on the 19th of April? Who was the addressee?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The chief at the time -- I mean, we addressed Mr. Amir Kubura as the chief at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, do you know whether Mr. Asim Koricic was at that time still in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember whether at the time he was in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to take you to Ovnak. Who was -- or there was a tactical group who was in charge of the overall Ovnak operation, and the tactical group was called Sedam. Have you heard about this?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I haven't heard of it, but I suppose my battalion commander, who was my superior, must have heard. I had not heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please just confirm, the soldiers from the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, they returned to Kakanj on the 9th of June, 1993, after the operation?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Were they accompanied by another battalion or were they just coming on their own? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: At first, members of the 3rd Battalion came and they returned to barracks, they collected their MTS and then they were directed to guard again. And I think immediately afterwards -- because for security reasons, you can't have a huge column of people going one after another, and I think that then it was the members of the 2nd Battalion who were also directed to go in the same direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to switch the topic and talk about a meeting on the 13th of May, 1993, so roughly five days before the events in Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher may have document P558 distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: These are meeting minutes from a meeting which you, yourself, attended on the 13th of May. And first of all, it states on the first page that it was a meeting of the brigade command and the Sura [phoen]. Do you recall having attended this meeting on the 13th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember the date, but perhaps if I could look at the contents and see what it was all about, perhaps I might remember. I can't tell you the date. I can't tell whether it was on that date or not. I really can't

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please have a look at the document. Your intervention is mentioned on the second page in the B/C/S version, and for the others, it's page 3 of the English version in the middle. But please have a look at it first.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: What I can recall is the following: Right before this meeting, a certain amount of MTOs [as interpreted] was determined in the course of combat activity as having been taken from the HVO, somewhere in the vicinity of Zenica. So we are talking about MTS vehicles and the equipment that had been used by the HVO forces and what was left behind when they withdrew before the units of the 7th Brigade. So it was the equipment that could have been used in order to replenish our own resources in terms of materiel and technical equipment, and all of that was indispensable for the carrying out of our tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And was this operation on Mount Smaljevac, and the HVO equipment, was it based in Cocuka? Does this ring a bell? An operation on the 25th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I did not take part in this operation myself. I was in Kakanj, but members of the Kakanj Battalion was -- were led and the commander was Mr. Catic, so I did not have access to documents as to the movements of the unit or any other details with regard to their movements on the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So Mr. Catic, along with a couple of soldiers from the 3rd Battalion, participated in it but you didn't?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your intervention relates to vehicles, your intervention during this meeting, I'm referring to --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I see my learned friend on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. My basic comment is that this is outside the scope of the facts covered by the indictment. This is an event from the month of April and -- I mean this event that the witness was referring to and the events that happened in the vicinity of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do you have to say for yourself, Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Certainly, this event is outside the indictment or it's not charged in the indictment itself, but it relates to the treatment of war booty by members of the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade and the Prosecution believes it therefore might demonstrate -- or might be relevant as a kind of background for the treatment of war booty within that brigade. And the witness has in the course of this meeting made a comment about it, and we believe since the author is here, he is best placed to comment upon this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right then. As to this context, go ahead and ask your question now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I can just -- or can you just -- it is mentioned here that motor vehicles were driven away from Cocuka and a question of registering came up. Can you please read out what you contributed to this meeting. Can you read out your intervention, please.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: When the war booty arrived at Kakanj, I did my best in order to make sure that it was all recorded and it happened, and all the vehicles were recorded and were under control, registered.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you please continue to read what Mr. Nesib Talic stated following your remark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I was going to ask the same question myself, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My learned colleague said that he would ask the witness to comment only on what he, himself, said in the course of this meeting, if my understanding was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Certainly the following comment was not made by the witness himself, but he attended the meeting and it is obviously in direct relation to what our witness had stated. And the Prosecution believes that this is, in fact, the best way to get the background of what happened and what was discussed during the meeting. We have an eye and an ear witness to the events. So with the leave of the Chamber, I would ask the witness to continue, read out the comment of Mr. Nesib Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you have the authorisation, because I was ask the same question anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please continue to read the intervention following yours, intervention of Mr. Nesib Talic?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Right, then. Nesib Talic: "All these problems are the result of the presence of Turks, Arabs, and guerillas. The security service will do everything to secure the return of all stolen vehicles. I propose that rules be adopted at this meeting to avoid such situations being repeated."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And having attended this meeting, do you know what this means, "the presence of Turks, Arabs, and guerillas," in relation to the stolen vehicles? What is the background?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: After such a long time, I can't recall details of that meeting. I'm reading the report of what people said here. All I can say is comment on what I, myself, had said, but in conjunction with this comment by Nesib Talic, I really don't remember what exactly happened at that meeting, whether he said this or not, I really can't remember. What happened in Kakanj in relation to the war booty, I can, of course, tell you about that because I was at the barracks and I do remember certain details in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please state where the vehicles were brought to. Was this to Motel Sretno? Where the warehouse was? Can you please tell the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: As to the aforementioned things, I mean those were vehicles, a couple of vehicles that were placed at the disposal of the battalion. And in order for that to be done, they had to be registered, as is indicated here. So what we were trying to do was the stuff that arrived to be placed at the disposal of the battalion and under control, and in order to avoid individuals using or misusing, abusing this property, because we were talking about equipment which was necessary enough to carry out our tasks and because the HVO forces used the same sort of equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know whether in summer 1993 an investigation was launched into the issuance of permits for vehicles within the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Whilst I was at the battalion, there were no investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In what period of time were no investigations? Can you please clarify.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Until I was wounded, until the 8th when I was sent for treatment and so I was no longer at the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you say later on, or let's say do -- are you aware that later on investigations were launched and why these investigations were launched?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
