utterances.text: Now, given the advanced time, I just want to ask you for training in Zagradje. At the end of May, do you recall being in Zagradje and staying with members of the 3rd Battalion in Zagradje for training?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was at Zagradje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I'm referring to a document, P564, and it's mentioned here that there was a camp site in Zagradje. Just can you clarify where was a camp site or was there a camp site in Zagradje and where were soldiers billeted in a village?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Soldiers of the 3rd Battalion were at the district school, which is at the village of Zagradje itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And does this mean that the training was also conducted at the school or - before, in your testimony during the examination-in-chief, you referred -- you wanted to have training in the mountains - was the training somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: When it comes to training, within the training plan we had quite a few things planned, in fact; but as I've mentioned before, it was not real and proper training for the simple reason that we had no conditions for that. For example, shooting exercises could be carried out safely at the shooting range at Bare in Kakanj and that was the only place. But since there are Croat villages in the vicinity, we decided we wouldn't do it in order to avoid it being misunderstood and in order to avoid this shooting, disturbing the citizens of Kakanj and the surrounding villages. And that was one reason. The other reason was that we did not have enough ammunition because we had to save it for combat activity. The training I mentioned in the mountains referred to the troops being taken out of villages and to spend as little time as possible in the suburban area or in the hotel. And so with that aim in mind, they were taken to Zagradje in order to have them spend as little time as possible in an area where there were roads and villages, et cetera, because the population of Zagradje is 100 per cent Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And did all training of the 3rd Battalion -- or was all training of the 3rd Battalion conducted in Zagradje or was it also conducted at other locations or was Zagradje the main training location?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Training was also taking place at a school in Doboj once we were there. So some of it took place in classrooms, certain lectures, and then at the gym, and some of it also by going out into the mountains above the school. And the second part that took place at Zagradje, the troops were taken out there and we also had some training within limitations. I mean, we had to consider the restrictions imposed by the area around the village of Zagradje. So we called it training, but it was simply moving troops out of a suburban area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: P564 states and I quote under number nine, "The deputy battalion commander shall be the commander of the camp site." I'm referring to Zagradje on the 22nd of May, 1993. Were you, in fact, giving the training or was somebody else giving the training, performing the training?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Training was done on the basis of available resources from the battalion. For example, within the JNA, I was trained as a cellular [as interpreted] to work with radars. There was no sea; there were no radars at Zagradje. So I used the services of my colleagues and members of the battalion, fighters, who used to be trained and work with this sort of equipment and weaponry within the JNA so that they could show the basic things: How do you take a gun apart, how do you put it together again, how do you clean it, because we didn't even have any special weapons other than rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You were the deputy commander of the 3rd Battalion since the 22nd of February, 1993, and there was another training of the 3rd Battalion members which was concluded on the 8th of March, 1993. Do you know anything about this training?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I referred to that training course; it took place in the primary school building in Doboj. It took place in the classrooms, and the troops were taken out into the field, into the mountains, to train there. So part of the training took place while I was there, and another part took place while I was with the troops in Bijelo Bucje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And did the troops, after being in Doboj, were taken out in the mountains, were they taken to Zagradje, if you can please confirm or were they taken to another location?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: In Doboj, that's January, February, and March, and in March, we had the events surrounding the hotel, and then in May, there were -- there was Zagradje, that's where I went in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, can please P533 again be distributed. I -- the Prosecution had given that already to the witness at the very beginning. This is the report, again for the record, on the 3rd Muslim Mountain Brigade Battalion work and implementation of tasks, and I'm interested in page number 2 of the B/C/S version and page number 3 of the English version. And there is a headline "The level of training and readiness."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you please read out the first sentence followed by that headline?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I can't see the subtitles in the original document, so I have to find them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Actually, it is page 2 of the B/C/S document but it says page 1 here on top of it. It's ERN 0181, the number on top on the upper right-hand side 0181-1268.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: That's page 1 here where it mentions the level of training and readiness. It's on page 1, not on page 2. I've found it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Page 1. With the cover sheet, it would be page 2. I apologise. Under the heading -- or under the last heading, can you just please read out the first sentence?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: "As regards the level of training and readiness of unit members on the 8th of March, 1993, they completed training with Iranian instructors."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you please explain what this means, "training with Iranian instructors"?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: While I was staying in the school in Doboj, and while training was being provided at that time, there were no foreigners who participated in the training. We only had staff members of our own from our battalion. As far as the reference to the Iranian instructors is concerned, when I returned from Bijelo Bucje, I heard that a group of two, three, or four men, I don't know the exact number, a group of such men attended certain lectures in some of the classrooms. They'd either come from Visoko or Sarajevo. As to whether one could call them instructors if all they did was to attend the training in the building, well, I don't know, but I think they were there for just one day. They were just passing through Kakanj. They expressed the wish to visit that building. They were in civilian clothing. I don't know what sort of a mission they were involved in. I'm now telling you about the information that I received in the battalion when I returned there from Bijelo Bucje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who gave you -- who provided you with that information?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I received this information when I spoke to the men in the battalion, men who had been to the school in Doboj. At that time, there was just this secondary form of activity that we did not pay much attention to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: My last question relates to the 20th of June, 1993, and I'm summarising here from Prosecution Exhibit P498 in the English version, it's on page 5. According to this document, and on page 5, significant changes were made in the composition of the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It's not on this -- it's another document. I'm just summarising to speed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And these significant changes related to the composition of the officers in the 3rd Battalion and the following officers were concerned: Your superior, Nihad Catic; you, as the deputy commander of the 3rd Battalion; the assistant commander for intelligence of security Fuad Kulovic; the 1st Company commander, Fuad Kadic; the 2nd Company commander, Refik Husika; and the Seval Omerspahic. All these persons terminated their officer positions, according to the document, and my only question is: Why did after the 20th of June, 1993, all these men in a row, so to speak, terminate their services as officers in the 3rd Battalion command of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to have a look at the document because the interpreter didn't manage to catch all the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Certainly. May I ask the registrar, it's P498.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to see the date so that I can know where I was at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Certainly. You will be provided with the document in a moment. I don't know in the B/C/S version of this document what page it is. In the English version, it is page 5 and it's basically a list of officers within the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. It starts with the command of the brigade, with the 1st and the 2nd and the 3rd Battalion. And I would ask you kindly to look only at the page referring to the 3rd Battalion. It simply states -- it provides dates --

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. I need to hear about the heading of the document so that I can see the date. This is just part of the document. I can only see tables here. I'd need to see the first page of the document or perhaps you could inform me of the relevant date. I think that you said that it was the 20th of June, 1993; is that correct? Is that the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Not the date of the document itself, but the date on which the mentioned six persons in the 3rd Battalion command ceased their functions as officers, according to this document.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: So on the 20th of June, I was wounded on the 8th of June. On the 8th of June, I was treated for a few days, I was in the barracks. I spent a few days in the barracks until I was sent away for medical treatment. On the 20th of June, 1993, I was no longer in the barracks. I was being treated because of the wounds I had sustained. So as far as that event is concerned -- you said that certain individuals were replaced, I don't know how many, but as far as that is concerned, I'm not familiar with the reasons for their replacement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: For the benefit of the Trial Chamber, can we please put the page on the ELMO so that it is being displayed to everybody in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would just like to clarify something. My learned colleague put a question to the witness when he referred to the document and said that certain officers were replaced. This document doesn't refer to any replacements; it just refers to certain changes. So this document, this question might confuse the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Defence counsel quite rightly points out that you told the witness that certain individuals were replaced or dismissed, whereas one might simply have the impression that there were certain changes that were introduced, that there was an exchange of posts. So why does the Prosecution claim that individuals were dismissed? Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: First of all, I wanted to clarify in relation to this document that in the third column of this document, the times of services or the period of services are mentioned, and there are a couple of officers -- if I may ask the usher to put the document a little bit down, yeah, thank you. There are a couple of officers who cease their service on the 20th of June, 1993. For example are the commander that's the first line, Nihad Catic, and there are a couple of dates, and I can read them out again if this helps for clarification. Again, I just wanted to speed things up. In relation to the second document, it becomes clear -- or the replacement becomes clear. If I may ask the usher to show document -- or to provide document P544. This is a document which is relating to this document, to the reasons why these people -- which may be relating to this incident, the document dating from 25 June 1993. It was not intended to show this document, but since the Prosecution was asked for clarification, this is a document dating 25 June 1993 from General Hadzihasanovic to the deputy commander of the SVK and it states, if I may quote, beginning of quote, "Pursuant to order of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade command" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, just a minute. We have two members of the Defence counsel on their feet. Let's hear the first lawyer. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. My learned colleague referred to the date, the 20th of June. This document is not dated 20th of June, and these are members of the 3rd Battalion as far as I know. I don't know why this document is being referred to. I think this is very confusing for the witness. If he can answer the question that concerns the first document, I think that will be quite sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With regard to the additional questions put by my learned colleague, I'd just like to say that the witness has already answered the Prosecution's questions on a number of occasions. He was wounded on the 8th of June, he went away for medical treatment, and he can't comment on events that took place afterwards, regardless of the document that is in question. To continue along this line seems to amount to making certain -- or presenting certain arguments, but such questions can't be put to the witness because they just confuse the witness. The witness has already said that he cannot testify about anything that happened after he was wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Prosecution has heard Defence counsels' objections. Defence counsel claims that the witness wasn't there on the 20th of June, as he had been wounded. And therefore, as he has already said, there is nothing he can say about the 20th of June, about what happened on the 20th of June. So what's the purpose of insisting on an event that resulted in the dismissal of certain members of the 7th Brigade on the 20th of June? However, one could ask him whether he found out that friends of his were put in a position which they had to leave their post. This is the type of question that you could put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Alajbegovic, may I ask you - and that's my only question - have you heard whether your former colleagues or why your former colleagues were relieved of their duties on the 20th of June? And if I speak about relieving of duties, I'm just referring to the officer's position.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I know that Nihad Catic was transferred to a certain position in the brigade, I think, and he was assigned a different post and he was replaced by Mustafa Hadzihafizbegovic, who was the new battalion commander for the other individuals, and I can't remember anything. I know that the commander who was reassigned posts within the brigade were redistributed. So I really can't say anything about these other matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you just please clarify. To which position was Mr. Nihad Catic transferred?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. He was the battalion commander. The command had its headquarters in Kakanj, and he was then reassigned to some position in the brigade. And as I no longer had contact with Zenica, since I was in Kakanj receiving medical treatment, I don't know what position he was reassigned to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you for answering all my questions, and the Prosecution rests.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We have another 10 minutes before we have our break. Any additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I just have a few questions that arise from the questions put to the witness by my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Alajbegovic, my learned colleague asked you a question about vehicles and registrations that were mentioned at a meeting. Were these vehicles captured from the HVO?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: As I have already said, I wasn't in the field when these vehicles were taken. But given certain traces on the vehicles, given the camouflage paint on the vehicles, you could see that the army -- an army had used them. And in this case, they had been captured from the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Were vehicles used by the army registered through a competent organ?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The municipal secretariat of national defence was involved in these matters because vehicles had to be registered if the -- if that hasn't been the case, it wouldn't have been possible to register them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's 5.25. We will now have a break. And after the break, the Judges will have some questions for the witness. We will resume at about 10 to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will now resume, and I have a few questions that I would like to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you have a look at document P558 again. On page 2 in the English version, and in the B/C/S version, it's also on page 2. Have a look at what Nihad Catic had to say on that page. It follows what was said by Dzemal Hadzic and it's -- and after Nihad Catic there's something said by Mahmut Karalic. Could you read out what Nihad Catic said.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: "The lack of organisation collecting booty stemmed from our lack of experience. The Arabs did not permit access to one ammunition and explosive depot. The corps military police," it probably says, "removed uniforms from one lorry. Four submachine-guns and a car trailer from Kakanj were not reported."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Catic's reference to Arabs, who apparently did not permit access to an ammunition and explosive depots, now who are these Arabs he's referring to there, in your opinion? How do you interpret what Catic says, as far as you can remember what took place?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember what he said at the time, nor can I remember what others said at the time. This took place a long time ago. But what I've just read out means the following for me. This information was presented by Nihad Catic; he obtained it somewhere in the field. No location -- no geographic location is referred to here. I don't know what location is in question because I wasn't in the field when these operations were being conducted; I was in the barracks in Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Could you have a look at the last page of the document and the list of individuals to whom this document was addressed. Who is the first addressee?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: It says that it is the brigade Emir [Realtime transcript read in error "Amir"]. Should I read through the other addressees in the list?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You told us that you were a member of the JNA, a member of the navy, you have certain military knowledge. So when a list of addressees is compiled, when you have the most high-ranking person who appears under number 1, and then the other individuals appears in order of importance. How would you explain that the Emir of the brigade is listed before the brigade commander? Is there anything you could tell us? Is there any explanation you could provide in the light of the document that you have before you? And I could put the same question to you with regard to another document that concerned a list of officers who were replaced. And as far as I can remember, in the same document, the Emir was the first addressee in that document. Do you have a military explanation for this?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The way I see it on the basis of the reference to the Amir of the brigade and on the basis of what I've found out in the course of my stay at the 7th Brigade, Emir was an honourary position. It was Mr. Karalic and there was a certain respect on the part of the fighters for Mr. Karalic. And the way I saw it, it was an honourary position or title for him. And since he was the first in the line of command, as we saw on the basis of that order dated the 25th of December, the way I see it is a kind of an honourary position in order to avoid -- since this person had certain merits for the brigade and we didn't want to keep him without a title.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are telling us it's an honourary post. If we look at the conclusion of this document, at the end of this meeting, decisions were made by Mr. Karalic, who -- and this basically runs counter to what the other members have mentioned with regard to possible problems with the guerillas, the Turks, and the Arabs, he, himself, indicated that the guerilla should receive some sort of recompense. And he even suggested that five -- that certain soldiers from your own battalion should get this sort of compensation, this sort of price. So how does it go together with the fact that this was an honourary title? Could you shed some more light on this. What does actually transpire from the reading of this document? But you will see that in the end, he suggests that one soldier should be awarded the Golden Lily. As far as you know, who was allowed to grant the Golden Lily? The commander of the brigade? The commander of the 3rd Corps? Or was it up to the president, Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: In this case when I was referring to Mr. Karalic, his presence was aimed at making certain suggestions with regard to certain activities, when it came to both the war booty and the attitude to our soldiers, and it was about certain activities in order to boost the soldiers' morale in order to bring it up to the satisfactory level in order to make sure that they would be in a position to carry out their combat tasks. That's the way I read this. In this respect, we've got this proposal -- yes, there is a proposal for one soldier to be awarded the Golden Lily, so this proposal should be submitted. As far as I know, these awards were normally officially awarded at a higher level. The proposals came from the unit level with an explanatory note, and then the actual decision was made at the high level of command. I wouldn't be able to tell you at exactly what level, but it was certainly not done at the brigade level, perhaps even above the level of the corps. It was the highest war award, so it was probably the staff of the army. And as I was saying, the lower units could simply send in their proposals and explanatory notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right then. Thank you. Could you now take a look at P533, which is the report by Mr. Catic. And I would like to ask you to take a look at page 2, somewhere in the middle of page 2 in your language the sentence starts by "takodje vedan od problema," one of the basic problems. Could you read out this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. What is the number of the page, 1 or 2?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 2 in your document. Thank you. And it's in the middle of the page, more or less. And the paragraph starts by "takodje vedan od problema" --

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also, could you read out this paragraph, please?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: "Also one of the problems we encountered in our work so far was also represented by the fact that quite a few candidates that were at the MOS unit exited that formation when the battalion was formed, since they understood the nature of this unit. One of the reasons for the appearance of this problem is insufficient level of information and misinformation as well as a calculating attitude on the part of these candidates. A considerable number of this personnel joined the MOS unit simply in order to avoid mobilisation and any other units and the departure for the front."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right then. This document refers to MOS as far as you know, what is this unit that is being referred to in this document? Because if you read through this paragraph, it seems to indicate that members that were members of MOS had left it in order to boost the numbers of your battalion and that those people, apparently, caused certain problems. What can you tell us about MOS?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The term "MOS" is a term which was used by the people, by the population. I believe that it is due to the following: There was a Serb army which perpetrated the aggression; afterwards, the HVO, the Croat Defence Council, and the HOS were set up; and at the same time, or rather before, there was the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. MOS was a term which was -- colloquial term used by the people, and the actual real term is the term that was referred to in another document, which refers to the Independent Trsce Platoon with a list of members with regard to mobilisation, and that was approved by the Chief of Staff, the chief of municipal defence staff at Kakanj, which, as such, was an integral part of the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina. So Nihad Talic in that period of time when that unit was being set up and all these documents were being created was not present here, and apparently he must have used this colloquial term which is used by the people in our area at the time. So this reference that you are asking me about, as to whether there had been any problems or not, initially certain members failed to understand that war was a serious business and what it meant to belong to a serious military unit. So that when units started -- when units started to take part in combat activity, we had some people who were killed and wounded. And I believe, I suppose that it was for this reason that some of those who initially expressed the wish to join the 7th -- or rather to join the battalion -- well, that must have been the reason why they've given up the idea, why they didn't want to join the battalion and be mobilised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right then. If you allow me, I'd like to come back to the matter of this Motel Sretno in May 1993. Obviously it's a long time ago, but you must know because the Defence must have told you that in the indictment it is alleged that people were detained at the Sretno Motel and that some of them were mistreated. Now, so as not to spring any surprises on you, let me just tell you that we've already had testimonies from witnesses who had told us what had happened, according to them, at Motel Sretno. Now, were you, yourself, present in Kakanj in the month of May, and more specifically, were you at Motel Sretno? Where were you on the 18th of May?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: On the 18th of May in the afternoon, I was in Kakanj but not at Motel Sretno. So in the early evening, I can't really remember what time when I got to the barracks, it was at that stage that I heard from fighters what had happened, basically that the incident with the detention and the fact that the military police were taken prisoner by the HVO, this incident had already happened and the fact that certain members of the HVO were also taken prisoner but the -- by the remaining military policemen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in this story that you were told, who were the people who had brought the HVO members to the motel? Were they your own soldiers or some other soldiers? Because in the indictment, it is indicated that it was the military staff belonging to your company. So I'm trying to see clear here, and I'm asking you whether those were your own troops who detained those people or was it somebody else because in paragraph 42(F) of the indictment, it is stated that it was the 3rd Company of the 7th Brigade. Now, what can you tell us in order to clarify things in relation to this matter?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Whilst all this was going on, I was not, myself, at the Motel Sretno. Upon my arrival, I was told that with regard to these people being brought in - I was informed about this by the members of the battalion - I was told that members of the HVO were brought in by the brigade military police, the remaining ones who managed to return after the incident at the Rampa. So at that stage, I wasn't told that anyone from our own battalion participated in this action with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who was the highest-ranking officer at the Motel Sretno barracks?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And who was the battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Nihad Catic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And did you, yourself, have an office at Motel Sretno or a place where you would spend time in order to have a rest or to carry out your administrative duties within the unit? Did you have an office of your own?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was a smallish office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And did you stay in that office -- I mean, for how long and when exactly were you at that office?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't have any fixed working hours. According to needs, unless I was out in the field or on leave or carrying out other duties which required certain contacts and communications and meeting people in town, well, unless I was doing all these other things, I would come to the office and do what I had to do there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right then. Because one of the witnesses told us that on the 19th of May, that is to say the day after the 18th of May, he was still there; and we do know that on the 19th of May, there was a meeting between the BiH and the HVO about this matter. Were you informed of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I was not informed about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you did not know that there was a meeting on the 19th of May between the HVO and BiH?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: When you asked me the question, Your Honour, I said I did not know about anyone else being detained at the hotel, but I did hear about the meeting. I did hear about certain talks or negotiations being underway and UNPROFOR was involved, but I myself was not personally involved and I don't really know where exactly the meeting was taking place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And did you talk about this matter with Catic, about what could have happened, at least on the 18th of May, did you discuss this with him; and as far as you know, did he submit a report to the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Both of us were involved and were making efforts in terms of initiating these talks and obtaining a commitment from the commander of the 309th Brigade in terms of striving for an exchange. And I don't have information as to whether he had ever informed any higher levels of command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this exchange, when did it take place, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, late at night these military police members were released late at night. One was brought in by UNPROFOR, and on the day after the HVO members were released. I don't know at what time. I think it must have been in the morning. I can't remember what time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And as far as you know, those HVO members who had been detained, they complained to you or to other battalion officers about the fact that some of them had been beaten?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, nobody complained of any mistreatment in the course of their stay at the hotel, so I'm not aware of any complaints having been made about their stay there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And did you know that on the 20th of May, that is to say two days later, a number of people who had been at Motel Sretno went to the Kakanj medical centre in order to be checked due to their state of health because of the fact that they had been beaten? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, after this exchange we concentrated on carrying out further orders and duties in conjunction with our own members, so we were not in touch with the medical centre and we did not get any information or any reports from them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right then. So you had no knowledge whatsoever about the medical follow-up to this situation, due to the fact that a number of people had been subjected to medical check with regard to their wounds. You did not know about it and -- would you like to reply?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right then. My last question: One witness, who himself was detained at that moment, came and testified and he indicated that the people who had detained him were the MOS people. And he said that they were wearing army fatigue uniforms and that their faces were smeared in black and so on and so forth. Does it sound credible to you that someone would say that they were MOS members, the people who arrested them, and not your military police? How -- could you explain that statement?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I did mention that the term "MOS" was widely used in the area; it was a colloquial term. As to what the witness in question had in mind when he said "MOS," I can't really say that. But what I do know is that -- well, I don't know whether this same person who had spent time at Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the motel, but if he was indeed at the motel, he must have been arrested by the police. As to whether they were wearing army fatigues at that time or not, since I wasn't present, I can't really make any statements about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Military police, have you ever seen any of them in person, military police officers from the brigade? Has it ever happened in the course of your duty there to come across anyone who was a member of the military police of the 7th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I most often came across them at the Zenica barracks because they were in charge of security at gates and checkpoints there, so that was where I saw them most often.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because the witness -- it was on page 1.570 and 71, and I'm saying this for the sake of the lawyers. The witness indicated that those MOS agents were wearing army fatigues and bandannas on their heads and green ribbons on their arms, armbands, and that their faces were smeared in black. Does this correspond to the description of the military police?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: A member of any unit can wear an armband or a ribbon or a bandanna and military police normally, as far as I can remember, even back then, they normally wear white belts. And I can't remember whether they had any other insignia or not, but they would be recognisable by the fact that they were wearing white belts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And about you yourself, on the night between the 18th and 19th of May, where did you spend the night, at home?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Until late at night, I can't remember when exactly, but until late I was involved in this communication process with the command of the 309th Brigade, and then I went home to spend the night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right then. Thank you very much. Now, I'm going to give the floor to the Prosecution and then to the others as well. We still have half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon again. My first question again relates to Mr. Karalic which was mentioned in the questions by the Presiding Judge. You stated that he was in the area of the -- or in the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. Where was Mr. Karalic based in 1993?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I saw that he was an Emir in the documents, and I told you what my understanding of the title Emir was. But as far as I was aware, Mr. Karalic was in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was he based in the Bilmiste barracks in Zenica or was he based somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: As deputy commander, I didn't have any contact with Mr. Karalic; I had contact with superior command. So I really couldn't tell you precisely where his office was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I can take you again to the meeting minutes from the meeting on the 13th of May, 1993. For the record, it's P558. Do you recall where that meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the meeting at which war booty was the subject of discussion?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, I do. The meeting you attended.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: It was held in the headquarters of the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So in Bilmiste, in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: In Bilmiste, in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. But this is the second or third time that confusing questions have been put. The brigade command was in Bilmiste; that is not in dispute. My learned friend asked whether it was located in Bilmiste or somewhere in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The Prosecution -- given that the witness attended the meeting, he can tell us whether it was in Zenica or Bilmiste. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution just intended to clarify. I want to move on to the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It says here under item 1 on the first page of the meeting minutes, Mr. Karalic, and I quote, "Explained the rules of distributing war booty according to Islam." That's the second sentence of the meeting minutes. Being at the meeting yourself, can you explain what is meant by "the rules of distributing war booty according to Islam"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. That doesn't fall within the scope of the questions that you put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I can allow this question to be put to the witness because I wanted to ask this question but I forgot to do so. It would be interesting to know whether there were rules or not because they are military rules. Were you aware of that fact that there's a document that refers to Islamic rules as well? Is there an explanation you could provide or are you unable to answer this question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to the Islamic rules on the distribution of booty -- well, as far as these rules are concerned, I haven't heard of them, and if there were any such rules, they should have existed in written form. I never saw such rules as to whether -- mentioned these rules or I really don't know. But I know that at the time, as deputy commander, according to my understanding of what I should do with whatever arrived in the barracks -- according to my understanding, it was necessary to register everything, ensure that such goods were not stolen, and I had to inform my superior command of all the relevant details, and that is what I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Presiding Judge asked you also for proposals made at the end by Mr. Karalic, proposals for awards. And if I read at the very last page of this document, I find above "Conclusion" the last sentence that "Mr. Karalic proposed that 25 soldiers from the 2nd Battalion should be awarded as well as 5 soldiers from the 3rd Battalion." This is certainly a detail, but do you recall why five soldiers from your battalion, from the 3rd Battalion, were proposed for awards?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember who these soldiers were, and I really can't remember whether they were given rewards. I don't know the criteria used by Mr. Karalic to select these five men. I don't know who participated in the operation. I don't know what the role of these five men was, but on the basis of the written documents that concern what Mr. Karalic said, these proposals were made to the brigade command. He suggested that certain steps be taken to raise the level of morale of the troops in -- with regard to carrying out combat tasks. So this, in fact, concerned ensuring that the level of morale was at an adequate level.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you look again at the last page and especially at the distribution list, you find that below the brigade Emir, the second person mentioned, is the brigade commander, the second person to whom these minutes go. To your understanding on the 13th of May, 1993, when this meeting took place, who was the brigade commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. My objection is identical to my previous one: It doesn't fall within the scope of questions that you put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In fact, I didn't put questions of this kind to the witness, but when I asked the witness why Emir was the first addressee and then the brigade commander was the second addressee, I asked the witness to explain this and the witness said that the title was an honourary one. Defence counsel believes that he has provided a full answer to this question, so please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Presiding Judge also mentioned or asked you for MOS and you elaborated a little bit about the background of MOS. If I can just ask you for clarification. Was there a group of MOS in Kakanj, and if so, please from what date to what date did it exist?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: So what do you mean when you mean "MOS"? What is your understanding of this term? In your opinion, who do you consider to be a member of MOS? If you can answer that question, I will be able to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm prepared to rephrase the question. I'm certainly not prepared to answer questions. The intention was to --

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise if I have failed to respect the procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, you haven't made any mistakes, rest assured. Mr. Neuner, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: My intention was just to clarify. The Presiding Judge mentioned that certain witnesses or one witness had referred to a person who was arresting him or a group who was arresting him as MOS, and you elaborated in your answer. You mentioned the MOS, what this concept meant for you. And the only question I have is: In your understanding, is MOS a unit which has a commander, and if so, was such a unit existing in Kakanj in 1992 or 1993?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were no MOS units, no such units existed. A unit exists if it has its own command, if it performs the tasks for which it was established. And there was no unit called MOS in Kakanj in 1992, 1993, or later on, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you heard about negotiations on the 19th of May, 1993, in response to a question by the Presiding Judge. Can you tell us: What did you hear about the negotiations taking place on the 19th of May?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing in particular, as far as I can remember. Reference was made to negotiations on the 19th; I think UNPROFOR, someone organised it. They spoke about when they were organised, who attended them. I don't know who attended them; I couldn't say because I wasn't there. I wasn't at the negotiations on the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You say UNPROFOR organised it. Are you referring to the Canadian Battalion or to a French Battalion of UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, at that time, the French Battalion was staying on the grounds of the Kakanj power plant.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I ask you to show Their Honours where the power plant was in Catici, the place you just mentioned, or the Kakanj -- you just mentioned the Kakanj power plant, excuse me. Would you be in a position to encircle or to show where the Kakanj power plant is on the map the Defence has produced?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I need the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please, with a pointer, show where the power plant was.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Here we have the abbreviation that's used in Kakanj, too, it's on the map. It says "TE," and then you have the facility that is marked here, there is the village of Kujavce on one side and Turbici on the other. And this where the Kakanj thermoelectric power plant is next to the River Bosna and this road here. It's right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please, with a marker, encircle it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, what is the purpose of the question, Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a technical objection, Mr. President. The witness already marked the map and signed it. When I asked the witness questions, they had to do with other matters, not with the matters that my learned colleague is referring to now. I have no objection to my colleague showing the witness another map which the witness could then mark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution, you don't have a map on you, do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We have a map. With the assistance of the usher --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Then the Prosecution will provide a map if it's the right one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Maybe it's not visible on this map, but Catici is visible.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: You can't see the thermoelectric power plant on this map; it's upstream the Bosna River, but you can't see it here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, sir, we don't have a map. Yes, Defence counsel, perhaps they could assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a map that could be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So the Defence is now assisting the Prosecution by providing them with a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please, again with a pointer, show where the power plant is?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I think that this is the same map, but the scale and format is different. We could compare them, if necessary. There's the Donja Banjevac village here, and then further down there's the thermoelectric power plant in Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's not the right map, but there is a larger map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To save time, I will withdraw my objection. The witness could mark the location of the plant on our map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's use the Defence's original map then. The Trial Chamber would like to thank the Defence for cooperating in order to save time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You would like me to mark the thermoelectric power plant in Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you could please make a 2 next to it.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. How far away, if you look at the map, is this power plant from Catici, just roughly?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Catici is here, and now we have two possibilities. You can talk of the distance as the crow flies, and then this route here, you can take the road. Which distance are you interested in?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: As the crow flies, maybe.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: It's easier for me if I try to remember this. The power plant is quite a large compound, and Catici is a large village and it has about 300 households. So from the periphery of the power plant to the village of Catici, I would say it's several hundred metres, a couple hundred metres. I used to work in the power plant, so I do remember more or less what the distance was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you heard on the 19th of May, 1993, that the meeting had taken place there, or did you hear that at a later point in time? The meeting I'm referring to is the meeting about -- or the negotiations you were mentioning earlier.

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the negotiations were held in the evening. Telephones were used extensively. UNPROFOR was involved. And if I'm not mistaken, on the following day rumour had it that these negotiations had taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to ask you a final question. The Presiding Judge asked you about the detainees held at Motel Sretno. Were you aware -- because you referred several times to HVOs, were you aware that also civilians were among the detained persons in Motel Sretno?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of there having been any civilians among the detainees.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Have you seen any of these detainees either being brought downstairs or brought upstairs on their way to the exchange?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: While the men were there, I never saw any of the detainees.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll give the floor to General Hadzihasanovic's Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no questions, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll now give the floor to Brigadier Kubura's Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, just a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you've had a look at the document P558. These are the -- this is the document from the joint meeting. If I remember what you said, you said that Mr. Karalic made certain suggestions, he didn't issue any orders?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: My second question with regard to this document is: Mr. Kubura was present at the meeting, as far as I can see on the basis of this document?

utterances.speaker: KASIM ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember Mr. Amir Kubura being present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no other questions, Mr. President, but for the sake of the transcript, on page 56, page 59, page 66, and page 69, when an Emir and Mr. Karalic mentioned, the transcript says "Amir" instead of "Emir." I just went to mention this for the sake of the transcript. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We won't confuse these names. Is Defence counsel tendering these maps into evidence? And then we will deal with the power plant.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. We would like to tender the maps marked by the witness into evidence as well as what the Prosecution used with the witness and there's the document dated the 25th of December, 1992, an order and a document of the -- dated the 5th of December, a list of men mobilised. These are documents we would like to tender into evidence. The witness recognised these documents and testified about them today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We have maps and documents. What's the Prosecution's position?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Hadzihasanovic's Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The first map will be admitted into evidence as DK53, this is a map of the Zenica sector. [In English] DK53 representing Zenica area. The second map is representing the area of Kakanj; it's admitted under reference DK54. The third document is a document entitled "Order," dated 25th of December, 1992, and is admitted into evidence under the reference DK55, with an English translation DK55/E. The last document is a document entitled "List of men that were mobilised on the 20th of October, 1992," and is dated the 5th of November, 1992 -- well, the stamp is dated the 5th of November and is admitted into evidence under the reference DK56 with an English translation DK56/E. [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So this completes your testimony. Thank you for having come to testify here on behalf of Brigadier Kubura's Defence. I wish you to safe trip home where you are currently employed in a certain company. I will now ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a few more seconds, but if there are no issues that need to be raised, the hearing will commence tomorrow at 9.00. As you know, two witnesses are scheduled for tomorrow, they are ready to testify, and I invite everyone to come back for the hearing tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 3rd day of May, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
